notes: Canada/France/Switzerland/Mexico/India current-fact reconciliation. Legacy low-cost retention claims were corrected where current provider evidence changed the lifecycle; all five remain HOLD/observation for the typical overseas-only OTP/retention job pending route-specific operational proof or because current acquisition/roaming constraints are explicit.

routes.acquisitionSummary: SpeakOut now uses an active-plan model rather than the legacy 365-day airtime-voucher model. The current physical SIM is CA$10; current plans start at CA$19/30 days and an annual talk/text plan is CA$125/360 days. Service is cancelled after 90 days with no active rate plan.

keep.action: Keep an active plan or purchase a new plan before the 90-day no-active-plan cancellation window ends. The cheapest currently listed monthly plan is CA$19/30 days; the old CA$25-per-365-day voucher rule is no longer the current service model.

routes.chinaActivation: Online activation is available, but SpeakOut service is restricted to Canada and current help/terms say it does not roam outside Canada. It is not an overseas OTP route.
routes.kyc: No credit check is advertised. Current service terms collect customer-identifying/contact information for activation; do not generalize this into a no-KYC legal claim.
routes.payment: SIMs and plans can be purchased online; account top-ups are available online by credit card or via Canadian 7-Eleven vouchers.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Not supported for the target use case. Current SpeakOut help/terms say service does not roam outside Canada and calls cannot be made or received outside Canada.
routes.refund: SIM cards and prepaid service credits are non-refundable under current help/terms.
routes.holdReason: Current product no longer supports the legacy CA$25/365-day retention model and does not roam outside Canada, so it cannot serve the overseas SMS/OTP job.
routes.tariffSummary: CA$10 physical SIM; current plans start CA$19/30d; account cancels after 90 days without an active plan; no roaming outside Canada.
guideSteps: Reference/HOLD only — do not use the legacy 365-day voucher economics.
For Canada-only use, maintain an active rate plan and never let the no-active-plan period reach 90 days.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Telcel Amigo supports physical SIM and online-delivered eSIM. The Aug-2026 prepaid contract says the line lifecycle ends after 365 days without activity and restarts with each Saldo recharge. New Amigo activation still requires the applicable initial package/recharge and mandatory line registration.

keep.action: Make a Saldo recharge before 365 days without activity. The current contract says the lifecycle restarts with each Saldo recharge, and current Telcel material lists prepaid recharges from MXN$10.

routes.chinaActivation: Telcel now sells Amigo eSIM online and allows installation over Wi-Fi, but all 2026 mobile lines must be registered before service. The general foreign-user registration page accepts a valid passport but also contains CURP language that makes a passport-only general-Amigo remote path insufficiently clear. Do not substitute the separate Tourist eSIM product for this route.
routes.kyc: Mandatory 2026 line registration. Telcel states foreigners may use a valid passport (or temporary CURP for foreigners), and remote registration adds a liveness selfie; the same page also asks for CURP information in all cases, so passport-only completion for ordinary Amigo remains a reviewed ambiguity.
routes.payment: Telcel supports online recharge and recharge from abroad; current recharge denominations start at MXN$10. Payment-method/country acceptance can vary by channel.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Telcel supports SMS while roaming. For U.S./Canada Sin Frontera use, prepaid lines must be active and prior Telcel-network traffic in Mexico is required; the service is not intended for permanent international use. Global inbound OTP reliability is not established by the reviewed evidence.
routes.holdReason: The lifecycle economics are attractive, but ordinary Amigo foreign-user remote registration remains ambiguous and route-specific long-term overseas OTP evidence is missing. Keep HOLD rather than conflating it with Telcel Tourist eSIM.
routes.tariffSummary: Current contract: 365 days without activity; any Saldo recharge resets lifecycle. Recharges start at MXN$10; mandatory 2026 line registration applies.
guideSteps: Use the ordinary Amigo route only after confirming your 2026 registration path; do not substitute Tourist eSIM evidence.
Recharge Saldo before the 365-day inactivity limit if retaining the number.
Verify the target roaming country and OTP service before relying on long-term use.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Jio prepaid non-use is governed by Jio’s current regulatory policy, not a fixed Rs.199/90-day recharge rule. After 90 days of continuous non-use, a line with main-account balance above Rs.20 enters Automatic Number Retention: Rs.20 is deducted for each additional 30-day non-use period until balance falls below the threshold.

keep.action: After 90 days of continuous non-use, maintain sufficient main-account balance for Automatic Number Retention. Jio deducts Rs.20 per 30-day extension; ten such deductions cover the remaining ~275 days of a 365-day no-use horizon, consuming about Rs.200. Any qualifying usage resets the non-use clock.

routes.chinaActivation: BLOCKER for typical remote acquisition: current Jio guidance sends new users to a Jio store/retailer with original identity and address documents. First-time IR activation should be prepared while the number is connected to the Jio network.
routes.kyc: New SIM activation requires original Proof of Identity and Proof of Address; current Jio examples include Passport. Aadhaar biometric eKYC is a separate path. The reviewed official flow is India-centric/in-person rather than an overseas-first path.
routes.payment: A usable prepaid plan is required for service; ongoing recharges/IR packs are managed through Jio channels. International payment acceptance is not relied on for this HOLD decision.
routes.wifiCalling: Supported on compatible devices, but not relied on for retention.
routes.roamingSms: Jio prepaid international roaming supports incoming SMS free of charge once IR is enabled. First-time IR preparation should be done while connected to the Jio network; an IR pack activates on first eligible foreign usage.
routes.holdReason: Current retention is cheaper/more flexible than the old Rs.199/90-day model, but India-centric SIM activation/POI+POA and first-time IR preparation make overseas-first acquisition impractical.
routes.tariffSummary: 90d non-use threshold, then Rs.20 automatic 30-day retention deductions while main balance is sufficient; incoming roaming SMS is free after IR setup.
guideSteps: Acquire/activate with valid POI+POA through the current Jio onboarding path.
Before travel, complete first-time international-roaming preparation while connected to Jio.
For pure non-use retention, keep enough main balance for Rs.20 automatic 30-day extensions after day 90.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Orange Mobicarte starts at EUR2.99 online. Orange’s current recharge table directly establishes line-validity tiers: EUR5 extends the line 1 month, while EUR10 and higher eligible recharges extend line validity 6 months. Mobicarte requires identity registration and the current offer is for people resident in or able to justify a stable link with metropolitan France.

keep.action: Use an eligible EUR10-or-higher recharge before each six-month line-validity period expires. Current Orange recharge tables explicitly show EUR10 recharges extending line validity by 6 months.

routes.chinaActivation: HOLD for typical overseas-only acquisition: current Mobicarte requires identification and is reserved to people residing in or able to justify a stable link with metropolitan France.
routes.kyc: Valid identity/identification is mandatory for prepaid Mobicarte; current offer eligibility also requires residence in or a stable link to metropolitan France.
routes.payment: Existing Mobicarte customers can recharge online by bank card 24/7.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Mobicarte can use international mode and current recharges include roaming in Europe on eligible products. Reviewed evidence does not establish the target long-term inbound-SMS/OTP behavior in China or other non-Europe destinations.
routes.holdReason: Retention economics are now verified, but France residence/stable-link eligibility plus unverified non-Europe inbound OTP behavior keep this route HOLD for the target overseas use case.
routes.tariffSummary: EUR2.99 Mobicarte Mini; EUR10 recharge extends line validity 6 months, about EUR20/year for retention; France-link/ID constraints apply.
guideSteps: Only consider the route if you satisfy Orange’s current France residence/stable-link and identification requirements.
Use an eligible EUR10+ recharge before each six-month line-validity period expires.
Do not assume China/non-Europe OTP reception without route-specific current evidence.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Sunrise Prepaid has no monthly fee; activation including SIM/eSIM costs CHF19.90 with CHF20 starting credit. Sunrise now directly states that a prepaid number is released after 17 months with no active use. Online eSIM registration can use a foreign address.

keep.action: Perform any qualifying active use before 17 months elapse. Sunrise explicitly counts a credit top-up, outgoing call, mobile-data use, outgoing SMS, or option/bundle purchase as active use. Online top-up starts at CHF10 and works abroad with a saved card.

routes.chinaActivation: Sunrise currently supports online prepaid eSIM registration with a foreign address and online activation. Physical SIM delivery is limited to Switzerland/Liechtenstein. Exact successful China-first registration/OTP use is not independently reproduced in the reviewed evidence.
routes.kyc: A valid identity document is required for prepaid registration/activation. The current travel-eSIM flow permits a foreign address; do not interpret this as no-KYC.
routes.payment: Online top-up starts at CHF10 and can be initiated in Switzerland or abroad; saved Swiss and foreign payment cards are supported subject to current limits.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Sunrise supports prepaid roaming. A current 2026 community troubleshooting thread states ordinary SMS should be receivable while roaming with network signal and roaming enabled, but route-specific China OTP reliability is not established.
routes.refund: Prepaid SIM/credit return is generally not available; current provider terms govern exceptions.
routes.holdReason: The old 12-month rule is resolved to a 17-month inactivity rule and foreign-address eSIM registration exists, but current independent China-first activation plus long-term OTP evidence is still insufficient for promotion.
routes.tariffSummary: CHF19.90 activation incl. CHF20 credit; number released after 17 months without active use; CHF10 top-up is one qualifying activity and can be done abroad.
guideSteps: Register the prepaid eSIM online with a valid identity document; foreign addresses are supported by the current eSIM flow.
Perform a qualifying active use before 17 months of inactivity; a CHF10 top-up is the lowest current top-up.
Treat China/OTP reliability as unverified until current independent evidence exists.
